studies.Reference: Nutrition and other risk factors for renal cell carcinoma in postmenopausal women.
studies.Title: Nutrition and other risk factors for renal cell carcinoma in postmenopausal women.
studies.Authors: Prineas RJ, Folsom AR, Zhang ZM, Sellers TA, Potter J
studies.Population: postmenopausal, predominantly white women in Iowa aged 55-69 years and free of cancer
studies.comparison_type: total dietary calcium; contrast not stated

sample_size.excerpt: Among 35,192 postmenopausal, predominantly white women in Iowa age 55-69 years and free of cancer, we collected baseline history, dietary information, and anthropometric data by mail in 1986. We ascertained the 8-year incidence (62 new cases) of renal cell carcinoma using the Iowa Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) register, the National Death Index, and mail follow-up.

cases.excerpt: We ascertained the 8-year incidence (62 new cases) of renal cell carcinoma using the Iowa Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) register, the National Death Index, and mail follow-up.

comparison.excerpt: Total dietary calcium was associated independently with a reduced risk of renal cell carcinoma.
